Spain tops the list of countries for digital nomads, while visa income thresholds are increasing

According to the Immigrant Invest Digital Nomad Visa Index 2026, Spain ranked first among over 50 countries with programs for remote workers. The assessment took into account tax conditions, income requirements, cost of living, visa duration, ease of application, and path to permanent residency. Following Spain are Malta and Portugal, then Germany and Hungary, with the UAE making it to the top six. The Spanish visa allows for a stay of up to five years with the possibility of transitioning to permanent residency upon meeting income conditions (approximately 200% of the minimum wage) and qualification requirements.

At the same time, several countries are adjusting their rules. In Thailand, by the beginning of October, 1043 Long-Term Residency (LTR) permits were issued to remote workers out of a total of 12,010 program recipients; starting from August 31, the Destination Thailand Visa (DTV) requirements have been tightened – now applicants need to provide proof of permanent residence in the country of application and a criminal record check. Malaysia is extending the DE Rantau permits for an additional two years for current holders. Tracker data shows that income thresholds for 13 programs are linked to local salaries and will be reviewed upwards in 2027 (Bulgaria will see an increase of approximately 12.6% from January 1).

Amid the expansion of visa routes (estimates of the number of countries with individual programs range from 40 to 60+), a new study by the RemoteLabour Index showed that modern AI agents currently automate only about 2.5% of real remote freelance tasks. The best model was able to handle work at a level acceptable to the client in only a small number of projects out of 23 categories. However, among the nomads themselves, the use of AI remains high – industry data shows around 89% utilization.

📌 Reduce-Only Orders: How to Avoid Accidentally Increasing Futures Risk

Main Points
⏺ Reduce-only orders can decrease an existing position but cannot increase its size
⏺ This setting helps prevent accidentally opening a position in the opposite direction
⏺ This post explains how one order setting can prevent an expensive trading mistake

1️⃣ Core Idea — with reduce-only enabled, an order can execute only against an existing position without increasing exposure.
2️⃣ Example — you hold a 1 BTC long position and place a sell order for 1.5 BTC. The exchange limits execution so the position cannot turn into a short.
3️⃣ Why It Helps — the setting is especially useful for take-profit orders, automated strategies, and multiple simultaneous exit orders.
4️⃣ Risk Surface — if the position is already closed, the order may be cancelled or rejected. Reduce-only doesn't protect against slippage or trading losses.
5️⃣ Practical Rule — check reduce-only settings when placing exit orders, especially if you use leverage or trading bots.

Final Thoughts

Sometimes trading risk comes from incorrect order settings rather than a bad prediction. Reduce-only helps close exposure without accidentally opening another position.

🚀 Gala Swap isn't just another DEX. It’s a powerful engine built to capture value directly from market inefficiencies, and it’s fueling a serious opportunity for liquidity providers.

Here’s the breakdown on why this is a potential game-changer, especially for new pools:

The Arbitrage Engine Is Already Running

Let's talk about that brand-new pool you just saw launch. How does it earn anything on day one? The answer is simple: Arbitrage.

The moment a pool goes live, its price can slightly differ from the prices on major centralized exchanges (CEX). Smart traders and automated bots, known as arbitrageurs, are constantly scanning for these tiny gaps. They buy where it’s cheap and sell where it’s dear.

This isn't theoretical volume. Even today, with only a handful of live pools on Gala Swap, millions of dollars in arbitrage volume are flowing through the platform daily. Every single one of those trades pays a fee to the liquidity provider (LP).

Real Volume, Real Fees (Not "Farm Token" Emissions)

This is what makes Gala Swap different. The yield isn't based on inflationary "farm token" emissions that you have to constantly race against.

The LP rewards on Gala Swap are generated by real trading activity—the essential work of keeping the DEX price in sync with the broader market. When you provide liquidity, you become the infrastructure that makes this flow possible, and you earn your share of the fees from that volume.

The Real Gold Rush: Expanding the Surface

The current volume is impressive, but here’s what’s truly exciting: the bottleneck isn't the demand from traders; it's the surface area available for the arbitrage engine to work across.

🔖 Australia proposes new crypto exchange rules for 2027 

📣 Australia has proposed new rules for cryptocurrency trading and custody platforms on October 15, 2026, with financial regulator ASIC seeking public feedback by November 27 before the country’s digital asset licensing framework takes effect in April 2027. 

📊 The Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) announced the consultation alongside Consultation Paper 392, which outlines planned requirements for customer asset protection, trading practices and financial resources. The regulator expects to publish final guidance in March 2027, giving businesses time to prepare for the new licensing requirements. Australia’s upcoming rules will bring more cryptocurrency businesses under the country’s existing financial services licensing framework.

⚡️ The Corporations Amendment (Digital Assets Framework) Act 2026 creates two regulated categories: digital asset platforms and tokenized custody platforms. Digital asset platforms hold digital tokens for customers and provide related services, while tokenized custody platforms use digital tokens to record customers’ rights to underlying assets.
